records.summary: The records show 5299 3rd St is within the Bayview Neighborhood Commercial District (NCD-BAYVIEW) and the Third Street Alcohol Restricted Use District. Under the current zoning rules a bar with an ABC Type 42 license is a conditional use here, requiring a Conditional Use Authorization. Critically, the Third Street Alcohol RUD at § 249.62(a)(2)(E) allows a new Type 42 establishment in the Bayview NCD only with Conditional Use approval. This address has recent history as Gratta Wines: in 2016 a wine bar was approved as accessory to Butchertown Gourmet restaurant, and in 2019-2020 the space transitioned to a grocery/wine-making use with a Type 20 off-sale license referral approved. Within 500 ft there is one active Type 41 license and one revoked Type 48 license; six registered food/drink businesses including four bars sit within 500 ft, signaling existing alcohol density on this block.

findings.text: Planning Code § 737 (in force from 7 April 2025) permits a Bar with an ABC Type 42 license as a conditional use in the Bayview Neighborhood Commercial District, not as of right.

The Third Street Alcohol Restricted Use District § 249.62(a)(2)(E) (in force from 7 April 2025) states that a new on-sale establishment with a Type 42 license may open in the Bayview NCD with Conditional Use Authorization, but is not permitted elsewhere in the district.

This address operated as Gratta Wines wine bar in 2016, approved as accessory to Butchertown Gourmet restaurant under the prior NC-3 zoning. In 2019 Planning approved a conversion to a grocery store with accessory wine-making and explicitly prohibited bar or restaurant use with seating, stating the space must operate as a specialty food store with no seating permitted.

A Type 41 restaurant license application at 5201 3rd St, 114 meters away, was denied in 2017 citing Planning Code § 249.62 of the Third Street Alcohol RUD. A Type 47 bar conversion at 5251 3rd St, 34 meters away, was denied in 2003 for lack of a change-of-use building permit and conditional use authorization.

The Third Street Alcohol RUD § 249.62(b) requires every liquor establishment in the district to provide outside lighting and keep advertising to no more than 33% of windows and clear doors, with a clear view of the interior from the sidewalk.
Four registered bars operate within 500 feet of the site, including the Jazz Room at 5267 3rd St (18 meters away), which holds a Type 48 license with status "REV PENDING" as of the records date.

approvals.summary: The applicant did not state whether the Type 42 license will be a new application to ABC or a transfer from another location or owner, and the records do not show the space's last permitted use, so the rules cannot determine which ABC and Third Street RUD license requirements apply.

findings.text: ABC Type 42 is a non-quota on-sale beer-and-wine license for public premises (bar, wine bar, taproom) where no food is required and no minors are allowed. ABC issues new Type 42 licenses directly, but nearly every city treats a Type 42 as a bar use requiring a conditional use permit or planning review before ABC will issue.

The Third Street Alcohol RUD § 249.62(a)(2)(E) allows a new Type 42 establishment to open in the Bayview NCD with Conditional Use Authorization, but the rule does not define what makes an establishment new versus a transfer. The description does not state whether the license will be a new application or a transfer, so this control is not decided.

One ABC Type 41 on-sale beer-and-wine restaurant license is active at 5273 3rd St, 1 meter away, issued 2 February 2021. One ABC Type 48 full-bar license at 5267 3rd St, 18 meters away, shows status "REV PENDING" (revocation pending) as of the records date.

In 2020-2022 Planning approved a Public Convenience or Necessity referral for an ABC Type 20 off-sale license at this address (5299 3rd St) for the grocery-store use approved in 2019. A Type 20 off-sale license permits packaged sales only, not on-premises consumption, and does not establish precedent for an on-sale Type 42 bar license.

ABC's daily status reports do not show the status on 28 April 2025 of one license within 1,000 feet at this address; it changed status two or more times since then and is excluded from the license counts and from determining what the space is used as now.

approvals.summary: A health permit to operate a food facility is issued by the Department of Public Health after plan review and inspection, without a discretionary hearing, and is allowed for a bar serving food.

findings.text: Every food or drink business in San Francisco needs a DPH health permit to operate, issued after the final inspection confirms the facility matches approved plans and a certified food safety manager is on staff. The FY 2026-27 fee is $470 for the permit application including initial inspection, with a $0 annual license fee for restaurants and bars through 2026-28.

Limited cooking (small plates, light food preparation) requires DPH plan review of kitchen layout, equipment, finishes and menu. The FY 2026-27 flat fee for a bar with prepackaged food or limited prep is $1,241 for 4.5 hours of review, with additional review billed at $276 per hour.
A DPH permit application is sent to the Planning Department for interagency review. Planning will confirm the proposed use is permitted or conditionally permitted before DPH issues the health permit.

findings.text: The description states 40 seats, but Building Code occupant load is calculated from the floor plan and can exceed the number of seats, so 40 seats does not establish whether the proposed occupancy is Group B (under 50 people) or Group A-2 (50 or more). A bar is Assembly Group A-2; a space for fewer than 50 people is Group B.

Planning approved this address in 2019 as a grocery store with accessory wine-making and food prep, explicitly prohibiting bar or restaurant use with seating. Whether that grocery use is still active or the space is vacant is not shown by the records.

A change from grocery to bar is a Planning Code change of use. A change from Group B (grocery, or bar with fewer than 50 people) to Group A-2 (bar with 50 or more occupants) is a Building Code change of occupancy. Either change of use or change of occupancy triggers a building permit with plans routed to Planning for zoning review.

Tenant improvements including a limited kitchen build-out, restrooms, ADA upgrades and any change of occupancy require a DBI building permit with plans stamped by an architect. Fees are a percentage of construction valuation, estimated at $800 to $15,000.

expected_conditions.condition: Outside lighting and window transparency: no more than 33% of windows and clear doors may be covered by advertising, with a clear view of the interior from the sidewalk, per Third Street Alcohol RUD § 249.62(b).
expected_conditions.basis: Planning Code § 249.62(b) is a mandatory operating requirement for every liquor establishment in the Third Street Alcohol Restricted Use District, not a discretionary condition. Every approval in this district must comply.

expected_conditions.condition: Hours of operation limited to close by midnight or 1 a.m., consistent with neighborhood character and to minimize late-night impacts.
expected_conditions.basis: Comparable bar approvals in San Francisco Neighborhood Commercial districts frequently impose closing-hour limits. The description states the bar will close before midnight, which aligns with neighborhood wine-bar operations and avoids late-night entertainment permit triggers.

expected_conditions.condition: Security and good-neighbor plan: maintain a logbook of incidents, post a community liaison contact, and respond to neighbor complaints within 48 hours.
expected_conditions.basis: SF Planning's standard conditions for Conditional Use Authorizations in alcohol-restricted districts include security plans, community liaison requirements and incident logs. The Third Street corridor has a history of alcohol-license enforcement and a 2017 license denial, so expect heightened scrutiny.

expected_conditions.condition: ABC Type 42 license limits: no minors allowed on the premises at any time, and the license permits only beer and wine service, not distilled spirits.
expected_conditions.basis: ABC Type 42 regulations prohibit minors and restrict service to beer and wine. This is a state license condition, not a city condition, but operators must comply and it affects the concept's target market and hours.

expected_conditions.condition: Food service maintained as stated in the application: the bar must continue to serve small plates or light food as described, not operate as a bar without food.
expected_conditions.basis: The 2016 Gratta Wines wine bar was approved as accessory to a restaurant, and the 2019 grocery approval explicitly prohibited bar use. Planning may condition the new approval to ensure food service remains part of the operation to distinguish it from a pure drinking establishment.

filing_playbook.action: Submit a written inquiry to SF Planning asking: (1) whether the space's last permitted use (2019 grocery store) triggers a Planning Code change of use to Bar, and (2) whether a new Type 42 license application will be treated as a new establishment under Third Street Alcohol RUD § 249.62(a)(2)(E).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Attach the 2016 wine bar approval (2016-002128MIS), the 2019 grocery approval (2019-003896MIS) and the 2020 Type 20 referral (2020-012156MIS) and ask Planning to confirm in writing: Is returning to a wine bar use at 5299 3rd St a Planning Code change of use requiring a Conditional Use Authorization under § 737 and § 249.62? Does § 249.62(a)(2)(E) treat a new Type 42 license application as a new establishment, or can the 2016 approval be relied upon? Request a pre-application meeting with the Conditional Use planner assigned to the Bayview district to walk through the site history and the Third Street RUD controls before filing.

filing_playbook.action: Form the legal entity with the California Secretary of State and obtain an EIN from the IRS.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File LLC Articles of Organization (Form LLC-1, $70) or incorporate (Form ARTS-GS, $100) with the CA Secretary of State online. File the Statement of Information within 90 days ($20 for an LLC). Apply for an Employer Identification Number (EIN) from the IRS online immediately after forming the entity; the EIN is issued the same day and is required for the bank account, business registration, seller's permit and ABC application. If operating under the DBA Gratta Wines, file a Fictitious Business Name statement with the SF County Clerk, publish once a week for four weeks in a court-approved newspaper, and file proof of publication within 45 days.

filing_playbook.action: Register for the SF Business Registration Certificate and the CA Seller's Permit, and obtain workers' compensation insurance before filing the Conditional Use Authorization.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register with the SF Treasurer & Tax Collector for a Business Registration Certificate ($55-$700 based on gross receipts plus $4 state fee) to obtain your Business Account Number (BAN); every other city permit requires it. Register online with the CA Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA) for a Seller's Permit (free, often issued the same day); ABC will not issue a license until the seller's permit exists. Obtain workers' compensation insurance from a licensed carrier or State Fund before the first employee is hired; several city permits ask for proof of coverage. Register as an employer with the CA Employment Development Department (EDD) within 15 days of paying wages; your payroll provider needs the EDD account number.

filing_playbook.action: File the Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning, citing Planning Code § 303, § 737 (Bar use in NCD-BAYVIEW) and § 249.62 (Third Street Alcohol RUD).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the CUA application online with site photos, a floor plan showing the 40-seat layout and limited kitchen, a description emphasizing the wine bar's role as a neighborhood gathering place serving small plates, and a good-neighbor operations plan. State that the bar will serve only beer and wine (Type 42 license), close before midnight, maintain outside lighting and window transparency per § 249.62(b), and employ a certified food safety manager. Attach proof of the signed lease or letter of intent, the Business Account Number, and a map showing the one active Type 41 license at 5273 3rd St. The application fee for a no-construction CUA is approximately $3,150 (CPI-adjusted from the 2023-24 schedule); fees rise with construction cost. Request Priority Equity Geography fee waivers if eligible under § 249.97. File at least 6 months before the target opening date to allow for the pre-ap…

filing_playbook.action: Conduct the required pre-application community meeting and post the yellow notice for 30 days during the CUA review period.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: SF Planning will schedule a pre-application meeting with residents and business owners within 300 feet. Prepare a presentation on the concept, hours, food service, and good-neighbor commitments (incident log, community liaison contact, no minors). Emphasize that this is a wine bar with food, not a late-night bar, and that the 2016 Gratta Wines operated here previously. Post the yellow notice on the storefront for 30 days as instructed by Planning; take date-stamped photos of the posted notice. After the meeting, incorporate neighbor feedback into the operations plan and file a summary with Planning. The Third Street corridor has seen alcohol-license denials (2017) and a revoked Type 48 (Jazz Room), so proactive neighbor outreach is critical.

filing_playbook.action: After the Planning Commission approves the CUA, apply for the ABC Type 42 license, submitting the CUA decision letter, signed lease, seller's permit, entity formation documents and the Planning Department zoning sign-off to ABC.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Complete the ABC online application for a new Type 42 on-sale beer-and-wine public-premises license. Attach the signed lease, the approved CUA decision letter from the Planning Commission, the seller's permit from CDTFA, proof of entity formation, a diagram of the premises, and the Planning Department's zoning clearance letter. Pay the ABC filing fee (approximately $1,000) and post the required 30-day public notice at the premises; take date-stamped photos of the posted notice. ABC will send the application to SF Police (ABC Liaison Unit) and SF Planning for referral review under California Business and Professions Code § 23987. Expect 60-120 days for ABC to issue the license if unprotested. If the census tract shows undue concentration of on-sale licenses, Planning may require a Public Convenience or Necessity (PCN) letter from the Board of Supervisors, adding 1-3 months; start that pr…

filing_playbook.action: Submit building permit plans for tenant improvements (limited kitchen, restrooms, ADA upgrades) to DBI with the kitchen layout, equipment and finishes routed to DPH for health plan review.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Hire an architect experienced with SF restaurant and bar projects to prepare stamped plans showing the 1,200-square-foot layout with 40 seats, limited kitchen (prep sink, refrigeration, small cooking equipment), handwashing sinks, three-compartment sink, grease interceptor (if required by SFPUC's FOG program), ADA-compliant restrooms, and accessible path of travel. Submit the building permit application to DBI online, listing the CUA case number and the approved use (Bar, 40 seats, limited cooking). DBI will route the plans to Planning for zoning compliance and to DPH for health plan review. DPH's plan-check fee for a bar with limited prep is $1,241 (FY 2026-27). If the occupant load exceeds 50 people, the Fire Department will require a Place of Assembly permit ($446) and posted occupancy sign. Address all DPH, Planning and Fire comments before DBI issues the building permit; incomplete…

filing_playbook.action: After the building permit is issued and construction is substantially complete, schedule the DPH pre-opening inspection and obtain the health permit to operate.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: When construction is 80% complete, contact your DPH plan reviewer to schedule a pre-final inspection; book at least two weeks in advance. Walk the space against the DPH checklist one week before the inspection: confirm hot water is working, handwashing sinks are stocked with soap and paper towels, all surfaces are sealed and smooth, food equipment is NSF-listed, and the three-compartment sink and grease interceptor are installed. Ensure at least one employee has passed an ANSI-accredited Certified Food Protection Manager exam (ServSafe or equivalent, $100-$250, valid 5 years) and all employees have California Food Handler Cards ($7-$15, valid 3 years). After the final inspection passes, DPH will issue the health permit to operate ($470 application fee, $0 annual license fee for 2026-28). timeline_cost.notes: The time and cost ranges cover the Conditional Use Authorization hearing (120-300 days from filing to approval, $3,100-$15,000 in Planning fees depending on construction cost) and the health permit to operate (14-45 days, $470 application fee plus $828-$1,241 for plan review). These are the approvals in the entitlement path when they are granted. The ranges do not include the ABC Type 42 license (60-150 days, $1,000-$1,600, handled in parallel after CUA approval), the building permit (14-120 days for plan review and construction, $800-$15,000 depending on scope), state and federal registrations (1-35 days, $200-$400 total), or sign and music licenses (7-45 days, $600-$5,000). The CUA timeline assumes no discretionary review requests or appeals; neighbor opposition or a discretionary review can add 3-6 months. If the census tract shows undue concentration of ABC licenses, a Public Convenience or Necessity letter from the Board of Supervisors may be required, adding 1-3 months to the ABC timeline. Start the CUA application at least 6 months before the target opening date. The total elapsed time from filing the CUA to opening the doors, including construction and all approvals, is typically 10-15 months for a new bar in San Francisco.
